title: Priority fallback for streaming TTFT regression across deployments
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers reported increased first-token latency and lower tokens/sec for streaming endpoints across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between the streaming backpressure path in the router and ensemble variant probing: when a streaming session spans >512 tokens and the router probes multiple model variants with different kernel latency profiles, inflight handshake/kv-cache pressure causes delayed first-token issuance and throttled token emission rates.

Impact: TTFT increased by ~12% and tokens/sec dropped up to 25% for affected workloads between 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC and 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. Affected customers include two enterprise VPCs and multiple hosted PLG users (incident refs below).

Hypothesis: The router's probing + warmup logic attempts parallel enqueue to multiple variants for quality-preserving routing. For long-lived streaming sessions the probe responses return at different times and the backpressure handling path serializes first-token completion when prefetch and kv warmup are both active, amplifying tail latency under moderate load. This is most visible for models/variants with mixed quantized kernels and heterogeneous context-window heuristics.

Short-term mitigation implemented: enable a feature-flagged "priority-first-token-fallback" that forces the first token for streaming sessions to be served by a single stable variant (fast-path) while background probing completes. For sessions where the fallback is used we disable prefetch of large KV pages until background probes finish. This gives immediate TTFT improvement for affected customers and is reversible via toggle.

Planned permanent fixes: 1) Add a router-level priority lane for first-token streaming paths that bypasses ensemble probe fanout, 2) improve backpressure isolation so KV warmup does not block streaming token emission, 3) add model-variant latency profiles into the probe decision so heavy-variance variants are deprioritized for streaming. These changes require runtime, router, and scheduler updates and will be staged under runtime-1.22.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use streaming chat endpoint with model ensemble routing enabled and at least one quantized variant with slower kernels; 2) Start a session with a ~800 token context prime followed by a short user prompt; 3) Under moderate cluster load (50-70% of baseline concurrency) observe first-token latency and tokens/sec compared to same session with ensemble disabled; 4) Reproducible locally by replaying customer trace: https://s3.redwood.ai/replays/INC-2026-47/trace-20260309.json
acceptance_criteria: Canary TTFT <= baseline + 5% for streaming sessions with context >512 over 24h
Tokens/sec regression eliminated (<=10% deviation vs baseline) for canary traffic
Feature flag allows safe rollback with no in-flight stalls observed
Telemetry added: per-session first-token path, probe fanout counts, and kv-warmup blocking metrics
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime and router PRs to release branch runtime-1.22-hotfix. 2) Enable feature flag 'stream_priority_fallback' in hosted for 1% of streaming traffic for 2 hours. 3) If stable, increase to 10% for 6 hours and validate TTFT/tokens/sec metrics. 4) Expand to Dedicated pilot customers (2 tenants) with on-call in watch for 24 hours. 5) Full rollout to all Hosted and then Private clusters over 48 hours. Monitoring gates: per-tenant SLO panels and error budget checks. Emergency rollback: toggle off 'stream_priority_fallback' and revert canary routing in 10 minutes.
notes: Trade-offs: the fallback improves first-token latency at the cost of temporarily serving the first token from a potentially lower-quality variant; customers with strict quality regressions will be contacted and offered dedicated routing. We need to balance model-quality SLAs vs SLOs for latency. Engineering estimate accounts for cross-team coordination (router/runtime/scheduler).
comments: 2026-03-10 Avery Chen: Initial triage complete. Reproduced TTFT delta vs non-ensemble on internal canary. Created feature flag design doc and experimental plan. Filed customer bridge notes (INC-2026-47).
2026-03-11 Miguel Ramos: Implemented prototype fallback in router branch 'feat/priority-first-token'. Benchmarked locally: TTFT improvement median -18% on synthetic streaming traces. Opened PR #689.

2026-03-11 Samir Patel (PM): Reviewed rollout plan; requested explicit per-tenant rollback procedure and emailed affected sales contacts. Added requirement to notify Dedicated customers before canary expansion.

2026-03-12 Priya Desai (SRE): Added Grafana panels for per-tenant probe-fanout and kv-warmup-blocked count. Added alert: probe-fanout > 3 AND ttft > baseline+10% for 5m triggers pager. Prepared runbook updates.

2026-03-13 Miguel Ramos: Deployed canary to hosted 1% at 04:00 UTC. Observed TTFT drop of 14% and tokens/sec recovery to within 8% of baseline for canary traffic. No errors increased. Proceeding to 10% per plan.
2026-03-13 Design review (Elena V.): Raised concern about UX parity when first-token variant differs from subsequent tokens — flagged as 'post-rollout UX validation' for product team.
